From: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@sirenflow.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency & errors on production (region-us-west)

Hi Monica,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 95th/99th latency and a burst of 5xx errors across our checkout flows hitting the Redwood endpoint in us-west around 07:50 PDT. Impact: slower page loads and failed tokenization for some users; customer severity: S1 for us.

What we've observed so far: 
- 95th latency went from ~120ms token to ~780ms token between 07:48–07:58.
- Error rate (5xx) jumped to ~6% for 10 minutes.
- Traffic pattern: small increase in concurrent sessions (+12%) but not enough to justify the regression alone.

We've attached a Grafana snapshot and a short logs bundle (sanitized). Can your team confirm whether anything changed on the model routing or a deployment happened this morning? We need an ETA for mitigation or a rollback.

We are ready to open an exec bridge if that's helpful — our CTO is standing by.

Thanks,
Sara Mitchell
CTO | SirenFlow

Monica — quick triage update from infra:
- No config rollouts scheduled this morning; last infra change was a kernel parameter tweak on 06/19 (not region-specific).
- Telemetry shows an increase in average KV cache miss rate for model X-v2 in us-west starting 07:46 — this aligns with the latency jump.
- We are seeing small spike in GPU memory fragmentation on a subset of instances (3/42 nodes) that correlates with degraded scheduling and slower token response.

Immediate mitigation options: 
- Temporary routing: divert a fraction of SirenFlow's traffic to model X-v1 (compatible) until we stabilize (fastest to implement).
- Node remediation: restart the 3 affected instances (risk: short-lived additional load during pod rescheduling).
- Increase pool capacity by spinning 8 additional instances in us-west for 15–30 mins (costly but low risk).

I'm recommending: 1) instant route diversion of 20% traffic to X-v1 + 2) restart the 3 nodes. That should get error rate under 1% within ~10–12 minutes if there are no downstream surprises. I'll attach a short logs excerpt and a timeline.

-David

- Preliminary effect: 5xx rate down from 6% to 0.8% in the first 9 minutes; p95 latency improving (now ~220ms token).
- Next: We will maintain the partial routing for 60 minutes while we run a controlled validation sweep. If stable, we will gradually return traffic to X-v2 over the next 2 hours.
- Internal action items: David's team will monitor memory fragmentation and run a heap-dump on the affected nodes; Karthik is validating model fidelity metrics for X-v1 fallback.

We're preparing a short post-incident note and will include a timeline and remediation plan. Sara — please let us know if your team needs a separate incident bridge or any additional artifacts.

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident summary: SirenFlow us-west regression — resolution & next steps

Team — final internal summary and recommended follow-ups: 
- Incident: transient latency and elevated 5xx (peak ~6%) impacting SirenFlow region us-west on 2027-06-21 07:46–08:05 PT.
- Root cause (interim): cache miss amplification on model X-v2 combined with GPU memory fragmentation on 3 instances leading to scheduling latency.
- Immediate mitigation executed: partial traffic diversion to X-v1 + targeted instance restarts at 13:12 PT; error rate reduced to <1% within 12 minutes; full normalization over 90 minutes.
- Customer communication: SirenFlow notified at 13:35 PT; post-incident note sent 14:20 PT (copy saved to Drive).

Action items (owners):
1) Engineering (David) — root-cause RCA + memory management fix and a preventative scheduler test (due 2027-07-05).
2) Model team (Karthik) — evaluate X-v2 cache pre-warming strategies and fallback verification matrix (due 2027-06-30).
3) CS (Laura & Monica) — finalize customer post-incident report and offer one week of extended observability retention for SirenFlow (proposal due 2027-06-25).

I'll file the incident in Jira (SUP-2189) and flag for the next reliability review. Thanks for the fast coordination.

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
